questions.question: The profit P (GBP million) made by a company t years after it started trading is modelled by P = (4t - 1)/10 + (3/4)ln[(t+1)/(2t+1)^2]. Show that exactly one year after it started trading the company had made a loss of approximately GBP 830 000.
questions.answer: P(1) = -0.828, a loss of about GBP 828 000 (approximately GBP 830 000)
steps: Substitute t = 1: the first term is (4 - 1)/10 = 0.3.
So P is about -0.828 (million pounds), a loss of approximately GBP 830 000.

questions.question: Show that the value of t for which P = 0 lies in the interval [6, 7].
questions.answer: P(6) = -0.088 < 0 and P(7) = 0.198 > 0, so there is a root in [6, 7].
steps: P is continuous for t > 0, since the logarithm argument is positive.
P changes sign between t = 6 and t = 7, so a root lies in [6, 7].

questions.question: Show that the equation P = 0 can be expressed in the form t = 1/4 + (15/8)ln[(2t+1)^2/(t+1)].
Using the iteration t(n+1) = 1/4 + (15/8)ln[(2t_n + 1)^2/(t_n + 1)] with t1 = 6, find the values of t2 and t6, giving your answers to 3 decimal places.
steps: Apply the same formula to t2 to get t3 = 6.2868.

questions.question: Hence find, according to the model, how many months it takes in total, from when the company started trading, for it to make a profit.
steps: The company makes a profit once P > 0, i.e. after the root t of P = 0.
Iterating to convergence gives t = 6.3149 years (agrees with the sign change in [6, 7]).
The profit is positive after 75.78 months, so it takes 76 whole months in total.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows part of the curve y = 6ln(2x + 3) - (1/2)x^2 + 4, x > -3/2. The curve cuts the negative x-axis at P. Show that the x coordinate of P lies in the interval [-1.25, -1.2].
steps: y is continuous on the interval and changes sign, so the root P lies in [-1.25, -1.2].

questions.question: The curve cuts the positive x-axis at Q. Using the iterative formula x(n+1) = sqrt(12ln(2x_n + 3) + 8) with x1 = 6, (i) find x2 to 4 decimal places; (ii) find, by continued iteration, the x coordinate of Q to 4 decimal places.
steps: x3 = 6.4082 using the same formula with x2.
Keep iterating until consecutive values agree to 4 decimal places.
The converged value is x = 6.4142, the x coordinate of Q.

questions.question: The curve y = 6ln(2x + 3) - (1/2)x^2 + 4 has a maximum turning point at M. Using calculus and showing each stage, find the x coordinate of M.
steps: The positive root (sqrt(105) - 3)/4 = 1.812 is the maximum (the other root is negative and outside the domain).

questions.question: Figure 3 shows part of the curve y = f(x), where f(x) = x(x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2). Find f'(x).
The line l is the normal to the curve y = f(x) at O and meets the curve again at P, which lies in the 3rd quadrant. Show that the x coordinate of P is a solution of x = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x/2)).
steps: Gradient of the curve at O: f'(0) = -(1/2)(8)(1) = -4.
The normal gradient is 1/4, so l has equation y = x/4.
At P: x(x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2) = x/4. Since x is not 0 at P, (x^2 - 4)e^(-x/2) = 1/4.
P is in the 3rd quadrant, so x < 0 and x = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x/2)).

questions.question: Using the iterative formula x(n+1) = -(1/2)sqrt(16 + e^(x_n/2)) with x1 = -2, find, to 4 decimal places, (i) the value of x2; (ii) the x coordinate of P.
steps: Each further step uses the previous value x_n inside e^(x_n/2).
Keep iterating until consecutive values agree to 4 decimal places.
The converged value is x = -2.0226, the x coordinate of P.

questions.question: The function g(x) = x^6 + 2x - 1000. Show that g(x) = 0 has a root a in the interval [3, 4].
questions.answer: g(3) = -265 < 0 and g(4) = 3104 > 0, so a root a lies in [3, 4].
steps: g is a polynomial, so it is continuous, and it changes sign on [3, 4].
Hence g(x) = 0 has a root a in [3, 4].

questions.question: Using the iteration formula x(n+1) = (1000 - 2x_n)^(1/6) with x1 = 3, (i) find, to 4 decimal places, the value of x2; (ii) find, by repeated iteration, the value of the root a, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
steps: Continue until consecutive values agree to 4 decimal places.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 4x - 12. Show that the equation f(x) = 0 can be written as x = sqrt(4(3 - x)/(3 + x)), x not equal to -3.
steps: Factor the first two terms: x^2(x + 3) + 4x - 12 = 0.
Divide by (x + 3), which is non-zero since x is not -3: x^2 = 4(3 - x)/(3 + x).
Take the positive square root (the root is positive): x = sqrt(4(3 - x)/(3 + x)).

questions.question: Use the iteration x(n+1) = sqrt(4(3 - x_n)/(3 + x_n)), n >= 0, with x0 = 1 to find, to 2 decimal places, the values of x1, x2 and x3.
steps: Rounded to 2 decimal places: x1 = 1.41, x2 = 1.20, x3 = 1.31.

questions.question: The root of f(x) = 0 is alpha. By choosing a suitable interval, prove that alpha = 1.272 to 3 decimal places.
steps: Let f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 4x - 12, which is continuous.
There is a sign change on [1.2715, 1.2725], so alpha = 1.272 to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: A curve has equation y = f(x), where f(x) = x^2 - 5x + e^x, x real. Show that the equation f(x) = 0 has a root alpha in the interval [1, 2].
questions.answer: f(1) = -1.282 < 0 and f(2) = 1.389 > 0, so there is a root alpha in [1, 2].
steps: f is continuous and changes sign on [1, 2].
Therefore f(x) = 0 has a root alpha in [1, 2].

questions.question: The iterative formula x(n+1) = sqrt(5x_n - e^(x_n)) with x1 = 1 is used to find an approximate value for the root alpha. (i) Find the value of x2 to 4 decimal places. (ii) Find, by repeated iteration, the value of alpha to 4 decimal places.
steps: From f(x) = 0: x^2 = 5x - e^x, so x = sqrt(5x - e^x).
Apply the same formula to x2 and then to each new value.
The sequence settles near 1.734 after repeated iteration.
Consecutive values agree to 4 decimal places at alpha = 1.7340.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x cos(x/3), x > 0. Find f'(x).
steps: Use the product rule with u = x and v = cos(x/3).

questions.question: Show that the equation f'(x) = 0 can be written as x = k arctan(k/x), where k is an integer to be found.
steps: cos(x/3) is not zero at a root (otherwise sin(x/3) would have to be 0, impossible for x > 0), so divide by cos(x/3): 1 = (x/3)tan(x/3).
Taking arctan: x/3 = arctan(3/x), so x = 3arctan(3/x) and k = 3.

questions.question: Starting with x1 = 2.5, use the iteration x(n+1) = k arctan(k/x_n) with k = 3 to calculate x2 and x6, giving your answers to 3 decimal places.
steps: Apply the formula to x2 to get x3, then continue in the same way.
Successive values: x3 = 2.5541, x4 = 2.5965, x5 = 2.5721 (values oscillate towards 2.58).

questions.question: Using a suitable interval and a suitable function that should be stated, show that a root of f'(x) = 0 is 2.581 correct to 3 decimal places.
questions.answer: With g(x) = x - 3arctan(3/x): g(2.5805) < 0 and g(2.5815) > 0, so the root is 2.581 to 3 dp.
steps: Let g(x) = x - 3arctan(3/x), which is continuous for x > 0.
There is a sign change on [2.5805, 2.5815], so the root is 2.581 to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: A sprinter's velocity v m/s is modelled by v = 12 - e^(t-10) - 12e^(-0.75t), t >= 0. Using calculus, find the sprinter's maximum velocity during the race.
questions.answer: Maximum at t = (10 + ln 9)/1.75 = 6.970 s, with v = 11.89 m/s (2 dp).
steps: dv/dt changes from positive to negative here, so this is a maximum.

questions.question: The sprinter runs 100 m in T seconds, so the integral from 0 to T of v dt = 100. Show that T = (1/12)(116 - 16e^(-0.75T) + e^(T-10) - e^(-10)).
steps: Integrate v: 12T - (e^(T-10) - e^(-10)) - 16(1 - e^(-0.75T)), since the integral of 12e^(-0.75t) is -16e^(-0.75t).

questions.question: Using the iteration T(n+1) = (1/12)(116 - 16e^(-0.75T_n) + e^(T_n - 10) - e^(-10)) with T1 = 10, find, to 4 decimal places, (i) the value of T2; (ii) the time taken by the sprinter to run the race, according to the model.
steps: Continue: T3 = 9.7306, then repeat until values agree to 4 decimal places.
The converged value is T = 9.7293, so the race takes 9.7293 s.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows curve C1 with equation y = 5e^(x-1) + 3 and curve C2 with equation y = 10 - x^2. The point P lies on C1 and has y coordinate 18. Find the x coordinate of P, writing your answer in the form ln k, where k is a constant to be found.
steps: Since 1 = ln e, x = ln e + ln 3 = ln(3e), so k = 3e (about 8.155).

questions.question: The curve C1 meets the curve C2 at x = alpha and at x = beta. Using a suitable interval and a suitable function that should be stated, show that alpha = 1.134 to 3 decimal places.
steps: At an intersection, 5e^(x-1) + 3 = 10 - x^2, so 5e^(x-1) + x^2 - 7 = 0.
Let h(x) = 5e^(x-1) + x^2 - 7, which is continuous.
Sign change on [1.1335, 1.1345], so alpha = 1.134 to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: The iterative equation x(n+1) = -sqrt(7 - 5e^(x_n - 1)) is used to find an approximation to beta. Using this formula with x1 = -3, find, to 6 decimal places, the value of x2 and the value of beta.
steps: From the intersection equation x^2 = 7 - 5e^(x - 1), and beta is negative, so beta = -sqrt(7 - 5e^(beta - 1)).
Each further step uses the previous value x_n in the exponent.
Iterate until consecutive values agree to 6 decimal places.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of the graph of y = f(x), where f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0. Find ff(6).
Solve the equation f(x) = 5x for f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0.
steps: For 0 <= x < 2: f(x) = 21 - 2(2 - x) = 17 + 2x. Then 17 + 2x = 5x gives x = 17/3, which is not in [0, 2), so it is rejected.
This value is at least 2, so it is valid: x = 25/7.

questions.question: Given that the equation f(x) = k, where k is a constant, has exactly two roots, state the set of possible values of k, for f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0.
steps: For 0 <= x < 2: f(x) = 17 + 2x takes values 17 <= f < 21.
For x >= 2: f(x) = 25 - 2x, which has maximum 21 at x = 2 and decreases.
k = 21 gives one root (x = 2); k > 21 gives no roots; k < 17 gives one root (x > 2).
For 17 <= k < 21 there is one root in [0, 2) and one root with x > 2 (for k = 17 the roots are x = 0 and x = 4).

questions.question: The graph with equation y = f(x) is transformed onto the graph with equation y = a f(x - b). The vertex of the transformed graph is (6, 3). Given that a and b are constants, find the value of a and the value of b.
steps: The vertex of y = f(x) is its maximum point (2, 21).
Under y = a f(x - b) this point maps to (b + 2, 21a).

questions.question: The curve C has equation y = x^2 cos(x/2), 0 < x <= pi, and has a stationary point at P. Show, using calculus, that the x coordinate of P is a solution of x = 2 arctan(4/x).
steps: dy/dx = 2x cos(x/2) - (x^2/2)sin(x/2), by the product rule and chain rule.
At a stationary point with x not 0: 2cos(x/2) = (x/2)sin(x/2), so tan(x/2) = 4/x.
Hence x/2 = arctan(4/x), i.e. x = 2 arctan(4/x).

questions.question: Using the iteration x(n+1) = 2 arctan(4/x_n) with x1 = 2, find the value of x2 and the value of x6, giving your answers to 3 decimal places.
steps: Apply the formula to x2 to get x3, and so on.
Continue to x6, applying the same formula each time.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows part of the curve y = 2cos(3x) - 3x + 4, x > 0, where x is in radians. The curve crosses the x-axis at P, and the x coordinate of P is alpha. Show that alpha lies between 0.8 and 0.9.
questions.answer: y(0.8) = 0.125 > 0 and y(0.9) = -0.508 < 0, so alpha is between 0.8 and 0.9.
steps: y is continuous and changes sign on [0.8, 0.9].

questions.question: The iteration x(n+1) = (1/3)arccos(1.5x_n - 2) can be used to find an approximate value for alpha. Using this iteration with x1 = 0.8, find, to 4 decimal places, the value of (i) x2; (ii) x5.
steps: Apply the formula to x2 to get x3 = 0.8068, then x4 = 0.8271.
Apply it once more to get x5.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows the curve y = 2cos(3x) - 3x + 4, x > 0. The points Q and R are local minimum points with x coordinates beta and lambda, the two smallest values of x at which local minima occur. Using calculus and showing each stage, find the exact value of beta and the exact value of lambda.
steps: dy/dx = -6sin(3x) - 3. Set dy/dx = 0 to get sin(3x) = -1/2.
d2y/dx2 = -18cos(3x). A minimum needs d2y/dx2 > 0, so cos(3x) < 0.
The first solution with cos(3x) < 0 is 3x = 7pi/6, so beta = 7pi/18.
3x = 11pi/6 has cos(3x) > 0, so it is a maximum and is not used.
The next minimum is at 3x = 7pi/6 + 2pi = 19pi/6, so lambda = 19pi/18.
